main_text.p: ptum prophanum censeant, juxta illud Mosis Ægyptii exioma tractat. Thephill. sect. 1. n. 11. כל דבר שצריך מעשה לשמו [illegible, ~3 letters] שהן הכותי פכול Quidquid necesse est fieri nomine tuo, si illud faciat Cutheus, prophanum est; sed hoc personæ, non characteris odio. Confimiliter falsum Judæis ne-fas esse legem κατὰ λέξιν in aliam lin-gvam transferre. Ipsi Talmudistæ Lin-gvam Græcam excipiunt, omnesque Judæi uno R. Azaria excepto Legem à 72. Interpretibus ex Hebræo textu ver-bum è verbo translatam fuisse testantur. Hic Azarias solus è Libris Chaldaicis Characterè Samaritano descriptis trans-lationem factam fuisse opinatur. Prætere-a R. Saadias apud Judæos celeberri-mus, ante sexcentos & quinquaginta an-nos Legem κατὰ λέξιν transtulit, quæ Thes-salonicæ ab ipsis Judæis charactere He-braeo excusa est, cujus exemplar penes nos est, estque Parisi. ejusdem translatio-nis exemplar Arabicis Characteribus ma-nuscriptum. page.notes: The Hebrew lines are set in the text column with no margin notes. Line 2 of the Hebrew contains a printed box-like glyph that I could not read; it is marked as illegible. The Hebrew and the Greek readings ("κατὰ λέξιν" in italic and roman) are my best reading of a small, slightly blurred scan. The Greek in the second occurrence and the first Hebrew line are uncertain. The page number and running head are reproduced as printed. The word "dices" is the catchword, so the text ends on "co-".
